No. The evidence shows only a small part of the property was cleared in 2021.

- Hansen tree-cover loss in 2021 was 81.3 ha, about 2.23% of the 3,643.5 ha asset.
- The JRC 2020 reference maps 98% of that area as forest in 2020, and later years were observed, so the event meets the corroboration rule.
- The MGAP 2021 forest map classes 68.1 ha as planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda), 0 ha as native forest, and 13.2 ha as outside mapped forest. This suggests the loss was mostly plantation harvest rather than conversion of native forest. The data can't confirm that on its own.
- A further 37.3 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha was not counted as an event. Even with it included, the total is about 118.6 ha, roughly 3.3% of the property.
